correctness.rationale: The exact delta-scattering ratio t/r=ik/gamma yields, up to a global phase, C_theta=cos(theta) sigma_x+i sin(theta) I. In quasimomentum, A=D sigma_x is a Hermitian involution, U_theta^2=exp(2i theta cos(q) A)+O(theta^2) uniformly in q, and unitary telescoping gives a vanishing O(n theta^2+theta+|n theta-tau|) difference for either parity. Contractive partial trace transfers state convergence. An explicit Bloch rotation yields the parity-dependent integral of sin(q)^2 cos(2 tau cos(q)); the Bessel identity evaluates it as J1(2tau)/(2tau), proving both matrices and entropy limits. Endpoint, zero and asymptotic statements follow from standard Bessel properties. The standalone check passed 244 independent direct Fourier, position-recurrence, quadrature and finite-size assertions; numerical tests are not treated as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The claimed contribution is the finite scaled-time two-parity Bessel formula for the reduced coin matrix and its entropy in a physically specified delta-scattering family. The 2026 source gives fixed-wavenumber asymptotics, 2011 gives fixed-coin asymptotics, 2005 gives finite-time numerical endpoint behavior, and the 2020 general two-step continuum-limit framework covers only the underlying dynamics. These statements do not assert the triangular physical scaling or evaluate its parity-sensitive entanglement. Searches of published research records and all accessible previous scientific claims did not identify a statement that subsumes this formula; this is a best-knowledge statement, not priority certification.
residual_risks: Undiscovered explicit finite-time coin-state Bessel calculation in older quantum-walk literature could cover the formula in an equivalent gauge; full global priority is not independently verified.
General two-step continuous-time reductions are previously known; any claim that those reductions themselves are original is excluded.
No claim is made about uniform convergence as the scaled-time variable tends to infinity together with the observation size.

value.rationale: The 2026 delta-scattering model identifies loss of uniform coin–position entropy convergence at vanishing transmission but does not resolve its physically natural time scale. Tuning measured incident wavenumber proportionally to inverse observation time yields an exact two-branch critical crossover, including a sharp 0-versus-1-bit parity distinction, a countable family of finite-time equality points at Bessel zeros, and an oscillatory algebraic envelope connecting to the known stationary value. These are observable quantitative boundaries absent from a fixed-coin limit, not a bare renaming of the established continuum-time evolution. The scope is one natural homogeneous model with a fixed localized preparation; utility is precise near-reflection calibration and finite-observation entanglement prediction.
